import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

It is registered as `research:202611/prose_prompt_wikilink_completion/prose_prompt_wikilink_completion.md` (`file:explicit:6076ac08ba06b3a51e27942e`). The commit is declared and the host makes it after this turn. I didn't touch the lead's `__final.md`, the drafts or the diagrams manifest.

**Layout:** the file opens with the title, a research-query blockquote, the infographic, then `## Bottom line` (the lead's verdict, plus the recommended-solution paragraph as `### Recommended solution`). After that come:
- Critique of the request
- Verified facts
- Requirement adjustments
- Recommended design: architecture, field model, keyboard contract, visual design, reliability checklist
- Scope and phasing: the allowlist, phases
- Open questions for Bryan
- About this report: the lead's byline listing the five input reports

There is no frontmatter, so there was no `updated_time` to update, and no heading is numbered.

**Content check:** a block-by-block comparison found every paragraph, list item, table row, code block and number from the lead's report in the new file word for word. The only exceptions are the intended edits below.
- The lead's hand-written section references (§5.1, §4.3, §6) are now links to the renamed sections.
- "Both defects above" became a link to Verified facts, because that section now comes after the critique.

**Links:** I added 12 in-document links. All of them resolve in both pandoc's Markdown and GFM output. The lead's report has no external URLs and no relative links, so nothing needed repair or was dropped. The infographic was confirmed beside the report before I embedded it.

**Diagrams:** the manifest's status was `ready`, and its `source` matches the lead's label. The `diagrams:` label wouldn't resolve (`unknown_kind`), so I read the manifest through its `file:explicit:78e58c389119466b6fa0fd2e` ref.

| Diagram | Anchor | Where it sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `controller-ownership` | `figure-controller-ownership` | after the three-bullet list under Architecture |
| `band-lifecycle` | `figure-band-lifecycle` | after the Field model list |

Both are byte-identical to the manifest, inside their figure `<div>`s, and each has one reference sentence linking to it. None were omitted. The file has two Mermaid fences: the lead had none, plus these two.

The lead also registered `fig-architecture.png`, `fig-membership.png` and `fig-keys.png`, but its report never mentions them. I left them out, because the only images I'm allowed to add are the infographic and the image agent's manifest diagrams.
